harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built a 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster (MariaDB 10.6.28 + galera-4) from scratch on node1/node2/node3 (RHEL7, no server packages pre-installed). Configured wsrep replication, opened firewalld Galera ports, bootstrapped the cluster, and loaded an application dataset (appdata.orders, 3 rows). Took the entire cluster down cleanly (node2, node3, then node1 last to guarantee safe_to_bootstrap), confirmed full outage, then restored it: bootstrapped node1 from its preserved grastate (seqno 9, safe_to_bootstrap:1) and rejoined node2/node3, recovering with all 4 committed rows (including a write made immediately before the outage) present and wsrep_cluster_size=3/Synced on every node. Then executed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured per-node boot_id + cluster/data health baselines, restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time via `sudo reboot` (never more than one down simultaneously), confirmed each node's boot_id changed, and verified each node auto-rejoined the cluster (size 3, Synced) with all 4 rows intact before moving to the next node.
actions_performed: Diagnosed RHEL7 nodes had no MariaDB server, no repos configured, and a hung 'yum -q check' process holding the yum lock on each node
Killed the stuck yum lock-holder processes on node1/node2/node3
Added MariaDB 10.6 upstream repo and CentOS 7 vault base/updates/extras repos on all three nodes
Fixed corrupted rpmdb on node1 (rpm --rebuilddb) after the killed process left it inconsistent
Installed MariaDB-server, MariaDB-client, MariaDB-common, MariaDB-shared, galera on all three nodes
Opened firewalld ports 3306/4567(tcp+udp)/4568/4444 on all three nodes
Appended CLUSTER_HOSTS to /etc/hosts on all three nodes
Wrote /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on each node with wsrep_cluster_address=gcomm://node1,node2,node3 and per-node wsrep_node_name/address
Bootstrapped Galera on node1 (galera_new_cluster) and started mariadb on node2/node3 to join via SST; confirmed wsrep_cluster_size=3, all Synced
Enabled mariadb.service on all three nodes for boot persistence
Created appdata.orders table and inserted 3 baseline rows plus 1 pre-maintenance-window row (4 total), confirmed replicated to all nodes

Performed a full ordered shutdown of the cluster (node2, node3, then node1 last) for the maintenance window; confirmed node1 grastate.dat had safe_to_bootstrap: 1 and all three nodes fully down (no mysqld processes)
Restored the cluster: galera_new_cluster on node1, then started mariadb on node2 and node3; verified wsrep_cluster_size=3/Synced and all 4 committed rows present on every node
Captured pre-restart boot_id and cluster/data health baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3 sequentially via backgrounded 'sudo reboot', polling each until reachable again
Verified each node's boot_id changed after its restart and that each node auto-rejoined the Galera cluster (size 3, Synced) with all 4 rows intact before restarting the next node

evidence.requirement: Baseline: 3-member Galera cluster running with application data before maintenance
evidence.summary: All three nodes report wsrep_cluster_size=3 and Synced; appdata.orders table created on node1 with 3 rows replicated to node2/node3, then a 4th 'last-write-before-maintenance' row committed on node1 just before shutdown.

evidence.requirement: Full cluster shutdown for the maintenance window
evidence.summary: mariadb stopped on node2, node3, then node1 (holding safe_to_bootstrap:1, seqno 9 in grastate.dat); systemctl is-active=inactive and no mysqld process on all three nodes confirms complete outage.

evidence.requirement: Cluster restored after maintenance with all committed writes present and all three members serving
evidence.summary: node1 bootstrapped via galera_new_cluster and shows all 4 rows including the pre-maintenance write; node2 and node3 restarted and rejoined, both reporting wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced, and the same 4 rows via SELECT COUNT/full SELECT.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence - node1: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id=bdbfa15c... with cluster_size=3/Synced/4 rows; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable during reboot; post-reboot boot_id=2d77fe51... (changed); mariadb active again with cluster_size=3/Synced/4 rows.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence - node2: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id=1a816f1f... with cluster_size=3/Synced/4 rows; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable during reboot; post-reboot boot_id=92f95aba... (changed); mariadb active again with cluster_size=3/Synced/4 rows.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence - node3: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state, final full-cluster health
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id=95e2f83d... with cluster_size=3/Synced/4 rows; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable during reboot; post-reboot boot_id=5d228d3b... (changed); mariadb active again with cluster_size=3/Synced/4 rows; final cross-check from node1 confirms wsrep_incoming_addresses lists all three IPs and all 4 committed rows are intact cluster-wide.
